title: {{ps_mode}} Net Logger
subtitle: The same live net log as Chapter 7, tuned for radios identified by unit number instead of amateur callsign — for {{ps_short}} nets, interoperability exercises, and served-agency support.

callout.label: QUICK VERSION
callout.text: Open the **{{ps_logger}}** from the dashboard. Click **+ New Net**, name it, pick a talkgroup and dispatch center, and **Create Net**. As units call in, type each **Radio ID / Unit #**, pick a **status**, and click **LOG ENTRY**. Click **Check Out** when a unit clears. Close the net and print the **📄 ICS-309** just like the amateur logger. If you already know the Amateur Net Logger (Chapter 7), you already know this one — the mechanics are identical.

blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The **{{ps_mode}} Net Logger** is the same live net log described in Chapter 7, set up for **{{ps_short}}** radio operations instead of amateur ones. The one real difference is *how a participant is identified*. On an amateur net, stations check in by **callsign**, which FieldCommand looks up in the FCC (Federal Communications Commission) license database. On a {{ps_short}} net, units check in by **Radio ID** — the unit number on a trunked, P25 (Project 25 digital public-safety), or conventional radio — and **no license lookup is needed or performed**. This is the tool for {{ps_mode}} nets, interoperability exercises, and any net where the participants may not hold amateur licenses.

For {{org_the}}, the {{ps_short}} side is branded as the **{{ps_logger}}**. Everything else — creating nets, logging entries, checking units out, the quarter-hour participation timer, Drill Mode, the Observer Link, and the ICS-309 (the standard Incident Command System communications log) export — works exactly as it does on the amateur logger. **This chapter covers only what's different; for the shared mechanics, read Chapter 7.**

callout.label: SAME ENGINE, DIFFERENT LABELS
callout.text: Under the hood the {{ps_logger}} and the Amateur Net Logger are the same tool. If you've run one, the other holds no surprises — the buttons are in the same places and behave the same way. What changes is the vocabulary: **Radio ID** instead of callsign, **units** instead of stations, and **talkgroups** and **dispatch centers** instead of frequencies and grid squares.

blocks.h1: How It Differs From the Amateur Net Logger

blocks.p: Here is the side-by-side, so you can see exactly which parts change:

rows: FCC callsign — auto-filled from the offline database
**Radio ID** (unit number) — typed in, no lookup
FCC lookup confirms an active license
By callsign → name and member ID
By radio ID → name and member ID
Radio ID in the station column

steps: On a device connected to the FieldCommand Wi-Fi, open the dashboard (default **http://192.168.50.1**).
Click the **{{ps_logger}}** — its header shows the blue **STARCOM** badge and reads **NET LOGGER**.

The logger opens with a blue accent theme. The layout mirrors the amateur logger: a net-picker strip, a two-column body with the logging area on the left, and a **STARCOM NET SUMMARY** sidebar on the right.

blocks.screenshot: The {{ps_mode}} Net Logger with the STARCOM badge header, the blue-accented net picker, and the summary sidebar

blocks.p: The navigation links at the top let you jump to the **{{ps_short}} Dashboard**, the **Amateur Logger**, or **Observer** mode. Until you create or select a net, the header reads **No Net Selected** and the body says *Select or create a {{ps_mode}} net to begin*.
Click the blue **+ New Net** button. The **Create {{ps_mode}} Net** box appears. Its fields are tuned for {{ps_short}} radio:

rows: A plain name for the net
Dispatch Net, Tactical Net, Command Net, Mutual Aid Net, Search and Rescue Net, EOC Coordination Net, or Medical Net
Labels the net and prints on the ICS-309.
Digital Talkgroup, Conventional Digital, Conventional Analog, P25, or DMR (Digital Mobile Radio)
The kind of radio channel the net uses.
The channel name or frequency the net runs on
The dispatch center backing the net (example: `{{county_ex}} Sheriff Dispatch`)
Optional; shows in the net header when set.

steps: Pick the **Type**, **Talkgroup**, and **Channel**, and name the **Dispatch Center** if there is one.
Click **Create Net**. The net goes active, a tab appears, and the check-in form is ready.

blocks.p: The **Log Unit Check-In / Traffic** form is where you record each unit as it calls in. Because there's no callsign to look up, you type the **Radio ID** and go — it's the only required field. The form's fields:

rows: The unit's radio identifier. Shown in bold, large type. **This is the only field you must fill in.**
The unit's name or the operator's name.
The unit's state: Check-In, Traffic, Priority Traffic, Emergency, Dispatch, Check-Out, En Route, On Scene, Available, or Out of Service.
Which talkgroup the unit is on: Digital Talkgroup, Conventional Digital, Conventional Analog, P25 Direct, DMR Direct, or GMRS (General Mobile Radio Service).
The channel the unit is using. The **📡 Pick** button lets you choose from your saved channels (ICS-205 / Channel Library).
Routine, Welfare, Priority, or Emergency — color-codes the row exactly as in the amateur logger.
A short free-text note about the unit or its message.
Optional. The unit's role on an incident, from the grouped list.
Optional. Ties the check-in to an incident and reveals a **📋 ICS-211 →** link to that incident's check-in list.

blocks.p: There's also a **📡 Dispatch Center** box at the top-right of the form. Type the dispatch center's name there and it shows in the net header, so everyone watching knows which dispatch is backing the net.

steps: Pick a **Status**, and add talkgroup, channel, location, or remarks as needed.
The unit drops into the **Units Logged** list, newest at the top, stamped with the time. Use **Clear** to reset the form without logging.

callout.label: NO ENTER-TO-LOG HERE
callout.text: Unlike the amateur logger, the {{ps_logger}} does not log on the Enter key — click the **LOG ENTRY** button to record each unit. Everything else about logging, including the colored precedence edge on each row, works the same.

blocks.h1: Checking Units Out, Traffic, and the Shared Tools

blocks.p: The rest of the {{ps_logger}} behaves just like Chapter 7, so we'll keep this short:

bullets: **Check Out** — each logged unit has a **Check Out** button and a running **Duration**. Click it when the unit clears; the time is frozen and rounded **up to the nearest quarter-hour**, the same way volunteer and staffing time is documented.

**Traffic Log tab** — the **📨 Traffic** tab records messages passed on the net (From unit, To unit/address, a Type such as Dispatch / Tactical / Resource Request / Status / Priority / Emergency, and a summary). This traffic is the primary content of the ICS-309.
**Sidebar** — the **STARCOM NET SUMMARY** panel shows the net name, type, unit count, traffic count, open/close times, and duration; the **ACTIVE NETS** panel lists every open net.
**Drill Mode** — the header checkbox marks the net as an exercise and raises the **⚠ DRILL / EXERCISE ⚠** banner; the exported ICS-309 is stamped accordingly. Always use it for training.
**🔗 Observer Link** — copies a read-only link so a supervisor or EOC officer can watch the net live without touching the log (Chapter 9).
**💾 Backup** — saves the whole net as a JSON file on your device.

blocks.h1: Closing the Net and Exporting the ICS-309

steps: Click the red **Close Net** button and confirm. **Every unit still checked in is automatically checked out** at the close time.
Click **📄 ICS-309**. The communications log builds, downloads, and opens in a new tab ready to print.

The printed form is labeled **STARCOM NET**, and its **Unit Check-In Log** shows the **Radio ID** in the station column (where the amateur version shows a callsign). It carries the net type, channel/frequency, open/close times, totals, the **Message Traffic Log**, and each unit's participation duration rounded up to the quarter-hour.

blocks.h1: Operators Who Hold Both a License and a Radio ID

callout.label: KEEP THE TWO LOGS CLEAN
callout.text: Some people carry **both** an amateur license and a {{ps_short}} radio ID. On a {{ps_mode}} net, they should check in **by radio ID only**, here. If they also need to take part in a concurrent **amateur** net on the same incident, they check into the **Amateur Net Logger** separately, by callsign (Chapter 7). Logging each person in the correct logger keeps both communications logs accurate and defensible.

bullets: __The net picker is stuck on *Loading nets…* or nets won't appear.__ The logger talks to the FieldCommand service on the Pi. Confirm your device is on the FieldCommand Wi-Fi and the server is running, then reload.
__I typed a unit but clicking LOG ENTRY did nothing / it asked for a Radio ID.__ A unit check-in needs a **Radio ID**. Type one in the Radio ID / Unit # field and log again.

__I only see amateur nets, not my {{ps_short}} nets (or vice-versa).__ The {{ps_logger}} shows only {{ps_mode}} nets, and the Amateur Logger shows only amateur nets — they're kept separate on purpose. Use the navigation links at the top to switch loggers.
__Log Traffic or Check Out said to select a net first.__ Click a net tab, or create one with **+ New Net**, before logging.
__The 📡 Pick button said no channels were found.__ You need an ICS-205 Communications Plan or a Channel Library set up for the incident. Until then, type the channel or frequency by hand.
__The ICS-309 export did nothing.__ Select a net first, then click **📄 ICS-309** again. If a pop-up was blocked, the file still downloads — check your downloads folder.
